content:
Heads up: this read is based on data as of 2026-03-28, 76 days ago, so treat the picture as a recent snapshot rather than live.

The ISA goal is funded at plan. Your free cash flow sits at £1,383/mo. The goal needs £1,009/mo at 10%, £1,071/mo at 7%, or £1,133/mo at 4%. The 7% figure is the working number — roughly the long-run average a broadly diversified portfolio has returned over a horizon like this, an assumption not a promise, which is why the 4% case stays visible as the stress test. At plan, £1,071/mo is covered with £312/mo to spare. The £12,000 already in the pot does significant heavy lifting through compounding over this horizon. The question now isn't whether you'll hit £40,000 by June 2028 — it's whether you want to get there sooner or build a buffer against the 4% stress case.

**Subscriptions** are running at £100/mo across the window. With only 10 transactions over 87 days the pattern is thin, but that category is the clearest discretionary line visible right now.

A trim of £25/mo from subscriptions won't move the arrival date materially, but it widens the cushion against the conservative scenario — every extra pound above £1,133/mo is stress-test cover.

[CTA:cut_lever]Trim 25 from subscriptions[/CTA]

— C.
